recipes.name: THANKSGIVING SIDES
ingredients: 1 cup all purpose flour (as needed to coat onions)
in Vegetable oil (enough to fry onions a cast iron)
instructions: For the Mashed Potatoes

Peel and slice large russet potatoes. Add them to a vacuum seal bag along with butter, heavy cream, salt and white pepper. Vacuum seal the bag closed. Place in a 194°F sous vide bath for 30-40 minutes. - 3 large russet potatoes (peeled and sliced) - 12 tbsp butter - Salt and white pepper - 1 cup heavy cream
Remove the bag from sous vide bath, open and pour into a fine mesh sieve into a bowl. Using a wooden spoon, push the potatoes through sieve.
Whisk minimally, just until potatoes and butter are combined.
Serve and enjoy.
For the Yams
Peel and slice your yams into ½ inch pieces, and then place in a well buttered casserole dish. Season with some kosher salt. - 3 yams (peeled and sliced)

In a bowl combine butter along with brown sugar, raw sugar, cinnamon, and freshly grated nutmeg. Stir to combine and then add to casserole dish on top of yams. - 12 tbsp butter - ½ cup brown sugar - ½ cup raw sugar - 1 tbsp cinnamon - 1 ½ tsp freshly grated nutmeg
Cover and place in a 375°F oven for 30 minutes. Remove from the oven, give them a good mix and then return to the oven, uncovered, for 15-20 minutes.
White the yams are cooking, add boiling whiskey to craisins and let soak. - 1 ½ cups whiskey - 1 cup craisins

Remove yams from the oven and give them a good stir. Plate them on a serving platter and top with dollops of ricotta cheese, toasted pecans, some whiskey-soaked Craisins, and a drizzle of honey. - 4 ½ tbsp ricotta cheese - ½ cup toasted pecans - Honey (for drizzling)
Serve and enjoy!
For the Green Bean Casserole
For the French Fried Onions
Start by cutting large onions in half and slicing them thinly using a mandoline. Place in a bowl and add buttermilk, covering the onions. Let sit for 15 minutes. - 2 large onions - 1 cup buttermilk
Drain onions and toss them in all purpose flour to coat. Once they’re nicely coated, use a fine mesh sieve to shake off the excess flour. - 1 cup all purpose flour (as needed to coat onions)
Heat up vegetable oil in a cast iron skillet to 300°F. Add onions and cook for 7-9 minutes or until golden brown. - in Vegetable oil (enough to fry onions a cast iron)
Remove and place on a plate lined with paper towels. Season with salt. Set aside. - Kosher salt
For the Cream of Mushroom Soup
Stem, smash and slice Cremini mushrooms. Then dice them into smaller pieces. - 8 ounces Cremini mushrooms (stemmed and sliced)
In a high walled sauté pan, add butter along with your sliced mushrooms and a pinch of salt. - 3 tbsp butter
Once the moisture has evaporated out of the mushrooms, add flour. Mix to combine for 1 minute. - 1 tbsp heaping flour
Add cloves of crushed garlic and cook for about 30 seconds before adding cognac to deglaze. - 2 cloves crushed garlic - 1 tbsp cognac (to deglaze the pan)

Once all the alcohol has cooked out, add chicken stock and heavy cream. Mix to combine and bring to a simmer before adding a dash of soy sauce. - 1 ½ cups chicken stock - 1 cup heavy cream - Dash of soy sauce
Cook until dark, thick, and rich.
For the Green Beans
Cut the stems off your green beans and then slice into 1 inch pieces. - 4 cups fresh green beans (ends trimmed)
Par-boil for about 2 minutes until bright green and then add to an ice bath.
After mixing them around to cool, drain the water.
For the Casserole Assembly
Combine green beans, cream of mushroom soup and ½ of the french fried onions. Stir to combine. - For the Green beans - For the Cream of mushroom - For the French fried onions
Butter a casserole dish and add mixture.
Cover and bake at 350°F for 15-20 minutes or until bubbly.
Remove from the oven, uncover, add the rest of the french fried onions and cook uncovered for an additional 5-10 minutes or until browned and bubbly.
Serve and enjoy!
